llm.summary: The skill’s core reporting function is coherent, but its subscription feature can install persistent jobs, stores the API key in a macOS LaunchAgent, and uses unsafe shell-built crontab commands.

dimensions.detail: Searching RedFox/Douyin tourism data, clustering it, generating an HTML report, and using a REDFOX_API_KEY fit the documented purpose; daily subscription is also disclosed, though it increases impact.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs agents to automatically open generated HTML and forbids --no-open for normal runs; generated HTML includes unescaped API-provided titles, URLs, authors, categories, and image URLs, so local browser opening carries avoidable content-injection risk.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no separate package installer beyond a documented pip dependency on requests and optional local API key configuration.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Normal operation writes reports under Downloads or a chosen output directory, opens a browser, calls redfox.hk, and reads a local env/config API key; these are mostly purpose-aligned, but the auto-open behavior and unescaped HTML are broader than necessary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The --subscribe path creates a LaunchAgent on macOS or mutates crontab elsewhere; macOS subscription may persist REDFOX_API_KEY in plaintext in the plist, and non-macOS cron install/removal uses shell=True with interpolated keyword/path.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust RedFoxHub and need recurring Douyin tourism reports. Avoid using --subscribe until the cron/LaunchAgent implementation is fixed; if you do use it, inspect LaunchAgents or crontab afterward and rotate the REDFOX_API_KEY if it was written to disk. Prefer one-off report generation with a chosen output directory.
llm.findings:
[AST4] unexpected: Verified: the cron install/removal paths build shell commands with interpolated values and shell=True. Scheduling is purpose-related, but this implementation creates command-injection and brittle crontab mutation risk.
[LP3] unexpected: Partly accepted: the artifacts disclose API key use, file output, browser opening, network calls, and subscription in prose, but there is no explicit permission block or clear privilege summary for shell/persistence behavior.
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: scheduled subscription and browser opening are documented in SKILL.md and READMEs, so this is not hidden tool poisoning; still, the persistence and auto-open details are high-impact enough to require review.
[SDI-2] expected: Accepted as a concern in context: subscription is a documented feature, but host-level LaunchAgent/crontab persistence is high-impact for a reporting skill and needs clearer consent and safer implementation.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded: natural-language invocation examples stay within the cultural-tourism Douyin domain; the concern is mainly that subscription should require explicit confirmation.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: daily subscription is disclosed, but automatic browser opening is mandatory in the skill instructions, and macOS subscription can place the API key into a persistent plist.
[E2] expected: Partly accepted: reading REDFOX_API_KEY is expected for authenticated API access; persisting it into a LaunchAgent plist during subscription is not adequately disclosed or minimized.
[OH1] unexpected: Accepted: the crontab removal command interpolates the script path into a shell pipeline, creating an avoidable shell-injection and overbroad removal risk.
[P2] expected: Not accepted as a security finding: the cited HTML comment is an ordinary font/CSS comment and control-byte review found no hidden instruction content.
[RA2] expected: Accepted as a review concern, not malicious behavior: persistence is explicitly tied to --subscribe and --unsubscribe exists, but host-level scheduled execution is high-impact and the implementation has unsafe shell and credential-storage details.
